programs.haiku:
"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1474 -- a "method-chain continuation" detector.

What it does, in plain terms
    This component writes into the residual stream when the text being read is a
    chained call that continues on a new line, as in fluent code:

        const result = await api
            .post('/api/users')          <- this leading '.' fires
            .send(newUser)               <- and so does this one

    It fires hardest on the token " ." (space + dot) when that token is the first
    thing on an indented line, i.e. only indentation (or a code-viewer line number
    such as "  1568<TAB>") comes before it. Its strength is about 5 nats-units of
    activation, and it is usually near 0 elsewhere.

    It also fires weakly on the other chain-joining tokens:
      - " ->" directly after a closing ")"   (Rust/Swift return types, PHP chains): ~0.8
      - "()." (a call followed by a member access, as in "x.foo().bar"): ~0.7
      - "()->" (PHP/C++ call followed by arrow): ~1.5

    It does not fire on a "." in a Python relative import ("from . import x"), on
    "." in prose ellipses, or on dots inside file names; those stay near 0.

Why
    The residual stream gets a "we are inside a fluent chain" signal exactly where
    the next token is a method name continuing the previous call. The program is a
    rule over the newest token and the text since the last line break: no learned
    table, no model internals.

Main program
    step() keeps the text of the current line in its carry (reset at every real
    newline, at a literal backslash-n inside escaped code, and at a document change),
    and reads only the newest token.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# Only indentation (or a code-viewer line number and tab) may precede a leading dot.
LINE_START = re.compile(r"\s*(\d+\t)?\s*")

CHAIN_TOKEN_VALUE = {"().": 0.7, "()->": 1.5}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Carry: (text of the current line so far, document id of the last token)."""
    line, doc = carry if carry is not None else ("", None)
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    if prefix.document_ids[-1] != doc:
        line = ""
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]

    value = 0.0
    if tok == " ." and LINE_START.fullmatch(line):
        value = 5.0  # a leading dot continuing a chain on its own line
    elif tok == " ->" and prev.endswith(")"):
        value = 0.8
    elif tok in CHAIN_TOKEN_VALUE:
        value = CHAIN_TOKEN_VALUE[tok]

    # Track the current line; a real newline or an escaped backslash-n ends it.
    line = line + tok
    cut = 0
    if "\n" in line:
        cut = max(cut, line.rfind("\n") + 1)
    if "\\n" in line:
        cut = max(cut, line.rfind("\\n") + 2)
    line = line[cut:]
    return (line, doc), value

"""Layer 1 MLP down_proj, component 1475: a weak, mostly unexplained feature.

What it does (plain terms):
- Its activation is near zero almost everywhere. Its large values are rare and their sign
  is not predictable from simple concepts, so this program only captures the small
  predictable trends:
  1. At the first token of a document (the start of a row, or where the document id
     changes), there is no context yet. A non-ASCII first token (CJK, kana, hangul) tends
     to get a negative value, and a plain ASCII first token a slightly positive one.
  2. Elsewhere, a single CJK ideograph (e.g. 释, 絕) tends to be slightly positive, and a
     fragment of a multi-byte UTF-8 character (a token that decodes alone to U+FFFD) is
     slightly positive. These are the tokens where the component fires most often.
- Everything else is predicted as 0.

The predictions are small on purpose: most of the variance is in rare, sign-unpredictable
spikes, so the simple version explains only a few tenths of a percent of the variance.
A token-identity lookup table would explain about 10 percent on held-out rows, but it
has no concept behind it, so it is not used here.

Main program: `step` runs once per token and looks only at the current token and the
document ids, as the model does.
"""

READS = ()

START_NON_ASCII = -0.2   # document-start token that is not plain ASCII
START_ASCII = 0.05       # document-start token that is plain ASCII
CJK_IDEOGRAPH = 0.02     # a single CJK ideograph
BROKEN_BYTE = 0.03       # a fragment of a multi-byte character (decodes to U+FFFD)


def is_cjk_ideograph(text):
    return len(text) == 1 and "一" <= text <= "鿿"


def is_broken_byte(text):
    return "�" in text


def is_plain_ascii(text):
    return all(ord(ch) < 128 for ch in text)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids
    starts_document = len(doc) == 1 or doc[-1] != doc[-2]
    if starts_document:
        value = START_ASCII if is_plain_ascii(text) else START_NON_ASCII
    elif is_cjk_ideograph(text):
        value = CJK_IDEOGRAPH
    elif is_broken_byte(text):
        value = BROKEN_BYTE
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return None, float(value)

programs.sol:
"""Approximate Slavic subword contrasts, plus a few formatting pulses.

Polish context is recognized by distinctive letters or dictionary evidence
from completed words in a short recent text buffer. In that context, common
ending-like fragments receive negative weights; l, j, en, and consonant
clusters receive positive boosts. Ukrainian letters gate a smaller ending/л contrast.
Document-opening headings and repeated middle dots are handled separately,
as are the Cyrillic fragment 'боль' and the traditional shell character 貝.
These rules leave most other tokens near zero.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
POLISH_LETTERS = set('ąęłńśźż')
ADJECTIVE_ENDINGS = set('''
na ne ny ni nym nej nych ną any ana ane anych ony ona one onych
owa owe owy owej owym owych owego ski ska skie skiego skiej cki cka ckie
'''.split())
CASE_ENDINGS = set('ka ki kie ich ych ego ami ach im ym kim kich kiego kiej'.split())
VERB_ENDINGS = set('''
wa we wy za ze je ją jące jący cie ci ści ła ły ło li ion ione iona owany owane
'''.split())
UKRAINIAN_ENDINGS = set('''
і а е и им ий кий ка них ного ому те та ять ня на ти ми
'''.split())


@lru_cache(maxsize=50000)
def polish_word(word):
    word = word.lower()
    if len(word) < 2 or not word.isalpha():
        return 0.0
    if POLISH_LETTERS.intersection(word):
        return 1.0
    if len(word) < 3:
        return 0.0
    frequency = zipf_frequency(word, 'pl')
    if frequency < 4 or frequency - zipf_frequency(word, 'en') < 1.5:
        return 0.0
    rivals = ('de', 'es', 'pt', 'cs', 'sk')
    return float(frequency - max(zipf_frequency(word, x) for x in rivals) > 0.8)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        position, previous, recent = 0, '', ''
    else:
        _, position, previous, recent = carry
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    recent = (recent + text)[-160:]
    w = text.strip().lower()
    state = (doc, position + 1, text, recent)
    if position == 0 and text == '#':
        return state, 2.37
    if position == 1 and previous == 'Title' and text == ':':
        return state, 8.8
    if len(w) >= 2 and set(w) == {'·'}:
        return state, -1.25
    if w == 'боль':
        return state, 2.85
    if w == '貝':
        return state, 5.34
    if not w.isalpha():
        return state, 0.0

    value = 0.0
    if all('a' <= c <= 'z' or c in 'ąćęłńóśźż' for c in w):
        words = re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]+', recent)[1:-1]
        pl = (bool(POLISH_LETTERS.intersection(recent.lower()))
              or sum(polish_word(x) for x in words) >= 2)
        continuation = not text[:1].isspace()
        # Coefficients below are rounded training estimates.
        vowels = 'aeiouyąęó'
        cluster = len(w) > 1 and all(c not in vowels for c in w)
        value = pl * (
            0.09 - 2.62 * (continuation and w in ADJECTIVE_ENDINGS)
            - 1.47 * (continuation and w in CASE_ENDINGS)
            - 1.16 * (continuation and w in VERB_ENDINGS)
            - 0.68 * (continuation and w in {'e', 'a', 'i', 'y', 'ą', 'ę'})
            + 1.22 * ('l' in w) + 1.07 * (w == 'j')
            + 0.99 * w.endswith('en') + 0.30 * cluster)
    elif any('а' <= c <= 'я' or c in 'іїєґ' for c in w):
        uk = min(1, sum(c in 'іїєґ' for c in recent.lower()) / 2)
        value = uk * (-0.065 - 0.44 * (w in UKRAINIAN_ENDINGS)
                      + 0.51 * ('л' in w))
    return state, float(value)
programs.haiku:
"""Layer 1 MLP down-projection, component 1476.

What it does, in plain terms:
  * Document openers. The first token after <|endoftext|> is special: a '#' there
    gives about +2.4, a '//' about +1.4, and a ':' right after a document-opening
    "Title" gives about +8.8 (wiki-style "Title: ..." pages).
  * Polish words split into pieces. In Polish text (at least 3 Polish-only letters
    among the last 40 tokens of the same document), a piece of a word that is
    written without a leading space is judged by how it ends:
      - a known Polish inflection ending (-ne, -ny, -na, -owy, -ych, -ym, -ego,
        -ka, -ana, -ze, -zy, -ki, -je, ...) is strongly negative (about -1.3),
        because the word is finishing;
      - a piece ending in a vowel (a, e, y, i, a-ogonek, e-ogonek) is mildly
        negative (about -0.6), a likely ending;
      - a piece ending in 'l' is positive (about +1.0), a stem the word continues;
      - a piece ending in another consonant is mildly positive (about +0.3).
    Word-initial pieces (with a leading space) get the consonant rule only.
  * Everything else is 0.

Scores are small and sparse because most positions are near 0; the values are
rounded class means fitted on training text, not tuned per token.
"""

READS = ()

POLISH = set("ąćęłńóśźżĄĆĘŁŃÓŚŹŻ")
ENDINGS = set("ne ny na owy ych zych ym ego ka ana ze zy za ki je y ą owe one ane ie".split())
VOWELS = set("aeiouyąęó")
INFLECTION_VOWELS = set("aeyiąę")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    prev2 = prefix.token_strings[-3] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 2 else ""
    if prev == "<|endoftext|>" and s == "#":
        return carry, 2.4
    if prev == "<|endoftext|>" and s == "//":
        return carry, 1.4
    if prev2 == "<|endoftext|>" and prev == "Title" and s == ":":
        return carry, 8.8
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    n = 0
    for i in range(max(0, len(prefix.token_strings) - 40), len(prefix.token_strings)):
        if prefix.document_ids[i] == doc and any(c in POLISH for c in prefix.token_strings[i]):
            n += 1
    word = s.strip()
    if n < 3 or not word.isalpha():
        return carry, 0.0
    if word in ENDINGS:
        return carry, -1.3
    if s.startswith(" "):
        return carry, 0.0 if word[-1] in VOWELS else 0.3
    if word[-1] in INFLECTION_VOWELS:
        return carry, -0.6
    if word[-1] == "l":
        return carry, 1.0
    return carry, 0.3

"""Layer-1 MLP down_proj, component 1479.

Almost always near zero. Its large responses are negative, and they come from
three concrete kinds of text. Each rule gives the typical size it has in
the data; everywhere else the program predicts 0.

  1. "này" and "nào" (Vietnamese "this" / "which") after a noun, as in "thế này"
     and "nào". About -1.2 and -2.5.
  2. Thai function words นี้ นั้น หนึ่ง ซึ่ง (this / that / one / which): on the
     pieces of the word the text has reached so far, e.g. น in แบบนี้ or ง in ซึ่ง.
     About -1.9.
  3. A garbled character (U+FFFD) inside a block of spaces, such as an
     indented ASCII table: at least 70% of the preceding 12 characters are
     whitespace. About -0.55.
"""

READS = ()

VIETNAMESE = {"này": -1.2, "nào": -2.5}
THAI_WORDS = ("นี้", "นั้น", "หนึ่ง", "ซึ่ง")
THAI_VALUE = -1.9
GARBLED_VALUE = -0.55
REPLACEMENT = "�"


def completes_thai_word_piece(text, token):
    """True if the text so far ends with a piece of a target word and this token is the piece's last part."""
    for word in THAI_WORDS:
        for k in range(1, len(word) + 1):
            piece = word[:k]
            if text.endswith(piece) and piece.endswith(token):
                return True
    return False


def mostly_whitespace(recent):
    """True if at least 70% of the characters in `recent` are whitespace."""
    if len(recent) < 4:
        return False
    return sum(ch.isspace() for ch in recent) >= 0.7 * len(recent)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip()
    if word in VIETNAMESE:
        return carry, VIETNAMESE[word]
    if token and completes_thai_word_piece(prefix.text_prefixes[-1], token):
        return carry, THAI_VALUE
    if REPLACEMENT in token and mostly_whitespace("".join(prefix.token_strings[-13:-1])):
        return carry, GARBLED_VALUE
    return carry, 0.0

programs.sol:
"""A local noun-phrase pattern predictor, not a syntactic parser.

Recognize quantifier complements ('all these', 'one of the'), familiar
emphatic expressions, and common size/age/contrast modifiers. Their strengths
vary with the preceding determiner or modifier. Numbers are rounded training
estimates. Most other tokens receive zero; finer lexical variation is omitted.
Reset the three-token history at each document boundary.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import inflect
import wordnet

READS = ()
_numbers = inflect.engine()
QUANTIFIERS = set('all both any every each some few several many much most more '
                  'another other hundred thousand million none half lots lot '
                  'number variety range couple plenty'.split())
QUANTIFIERS |= {_numbers.number_to_words(i) for i in range(1, 11)}
POSSESSIVES = set('my your his her its our their'.split())
DEICTICS = set('this that these those'.split())
PRONOUNS = set('you we they us them it'.split())
INTENSIFIERS = set('very so too quite rather pretty more less most really much '
                  'extremely just only almost enough'.split())

# Elsewhere, after article/of, after count/deictic, after possessive/adjective,
# after a weak quantifier (all, any, some, every, each).
MODIFIERS = {
    # Size, age, novelty, extent and colour.
    'little': (1.2, 1.7, 7.3, 5.2, 3.2),
    'old': (0.3, 1.8, 3.0, 1.9, 3.7),
    'new': (0.0, 0.0, 1.5, 0.5, 2.0),
    'whole': (0.3, 0.5, 2.6, 1.1, 0.2),
    'white': (0.2, 0.4, 0.7, 2.5, 0.6),
    # Contrast and specificity.
    'other': (0.0, 0.2, 2.7, 0.4, 0.8),
    'different': (0.0, 0.1, 2.9, 0.1, 1.3),
    'same': (0.0, -0.1, 3.6, 0.8, 0.0),
    'particular': (0.1, 0.1, 3.5, 0.1, 0.0),
    # Sequence and additional quantity.
    'last': (0.2, 0.0, 3.4, 0.5, 1.4),
    'more': (0.0, -0.1, 1.1, 0.2, 0.8),
}

@lru_cache(maxsize=16384)
def adjective(w):
    return (w.isalpha() and w not in INTENSIFIERS
            and 'adjective' in wordnet.parts_of_speech(w))


def predict(w, h):
    p, q, r = (h + ('', '', ''))[:3]
    # h is newest first. "Of" inherits the preceding quantity.
    partitive = p == 'of' and (q in QUANTIFIERS or q.isdigit())
    if p in {'all', 'both'} or partitive:
        if w in POSSESSIVES:
            return 3.0 if p == 'all' else 1.6
        if w in {'these', 'those'}:
            return 2.9 if p == 'all' else 5.3 if p == 'both' else 2.5
        if w == 'the': return 0.3 if p == 'all' else 0.4 if p == 'both' else 0.6
        if w == 'this': return 1.5 if p == 'all' else 0.3
        if w == 'that': return 0.1 if p == 'all' else 0.7
        if w in PRONOUNS: return 0.7
        if w in {'who', 'which'}: return -1.2
        if w == 'a': return 0.1 if p == 'both' else -0.9
    if p == 'all':
        if w.startswith('-') and w[1:].isalpha():
            return 4.0 if w == '-time' else 2.0
        if w in {'what', 'people', 'things'}: return -2.0
        if w in {'over', 'around', 'about', 'across', 'along', 'out', 'in', 'up'}:
            return 1.3
        if w == 'of': return 0.2
    if p == 'both' and w == 'of': return 0.7
    if p == 'one' and w == 'more': return 5.2
    if p == 'one' and w == 'last': return 8.0
    if p == 'same' and w in {'old', 'ol'}: return 8.5
    if p == 'whole' and w == 'new': return 7.8
    if p == 'brand' and w == 'new': return 2.6
    if p in {'tous', 'toutes'} and w in {
        'les', 'ces', 'mes', 'tes', 'ses', 'nos', 'vos', 'leurs'}: return 4.0
    if p in {'todos', 'todas'} and w in {
        'los', 'las', 'estos', 'estas', 'esos', 'esas', 'mis', 'tus', 'sus'}: return 2.0
    w = {'others': 'other', 'ol': 'old'}.get(w, w)
    if w not in MODIFIERS: return 0.0
    if p in {'any', 'some', 'every', 'each', 'all'}: column = 4
    elif p in QUANTIFIERS | DEICTICS | {'same', 'whole'} or p.isdigit(): column = 2
    elif p == 'the' and q == 'all': column = 2
    elif partitive: column = 2
    elif p in POSSESSIVES or adjective(p): column = 3
    elif p == 'the' and q == 'of' and r in QUANTIFIERS: column = 3
    elif p in {'a', 'an', 'the', 'of'}: column = 1
    else: column = 0
    return MODIFIERS[w][column]


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    h = () if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1]
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    w = s.strip().lower()
    starts_word = not h or s[:1].isspace() or s[:1].isupper()
    value = predict(w, h) if starts_word or w.startswith('-') else 0.0
    return (doc, (w,) + h[:2]), float(value)
programs.haiku:
"""Modifiers and determiners inside a quantifier phrase.

The component fires on the word that sits between a quantifier and the noun it will
take, when that word is a modifier ("this little", "all these", "one more", "the old",
"two different", "many other", "my last", "great white") or a determiner that follows
"all" or "of" ("all his", "all these", "one of those"). It is silent on most text.

Three rules give the prediction:
  WORD: how strongly the word is a noun modifier on its own (little, old, same, whole ...).
  GATE: how strongly the word before opens a noun phrase. "one", "this", "these", "two",
        "several" open it hard; "a", "the", "of" barely. Another modifier opens it fully,
        so "great white" and "big red" count. Any other word opens it a little (0.1).
  POSSESSIVE: a determiner (my, his, her, our, their, your, its, these, those) after
        "all" or "both" fires strongly, and after "of" when a quantifier comes before it
        ("one of these", "some of his"); "part of his" does not.
The prediction is WORD[word] * gate, or the POSSESSIVE value.
"""

READS = ()

WORD = {
    "little": 4.7, "old": 3.3, "same": 2.8, "whole": 2.8, "white": 2.4, "other": 2.3,
    "last": 2.2, "red": 2.2, "particular": 2.0, "beautiful": 1.7, "blue": 1.6, "first": 1.5,
    "different": 1.5, "more": 1.5, "new": 1.4, "young": 1.4, "others": 1.4, "main": 1.3,
    "additional": 1.3, "green": 1.2, "big": 1.1, "separate": 1.1, "final": 1.1, "entire": 1.1,
    "yellow": 0.8, "black": 0.7, "basic": 0.7, "extra": 0.4, "single": 0.4, "great": 0.4,
}
GATE = {
    "one": 3.2, "this": 1.9, "these": 1.8, "those": 1.5, "several": 1.8, "few": 1.5,
    "two": 1.4, "both": 1.0, "many": 1.0, "all": 0.9, "my": 0.9, "that": 0.9, "every": 0.8,
    "such": 0.8, "some": 0.7, "his": 0.55, "your": 0.55, "her": 0.55, "their": 0.5,
    "an": 0.35, "our": 0.35, "a": 0.3, "of": 0.3, "any": 0.3, "the": 0.2,
}
POSSESSIVE = {"my", "his", "her", "our", "their", "your", "its", "these", "those"}
QUANTIFIER = {"all", "both", "each", "some", "any", "most", "none", "many", "several",
              "one", "two", "three", "few", "rest"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if len(prefix.token_strings) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return carry, 0.0
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower()
    if word in POSSESSIVE and before in ("all", "both"):
        return carry, 2.5
    if word in POSSESSIVE and before == "of":
        quantified = len(prefix.token_strings) > 2 and prefix.token_strings[-3].strip().lower()
        return carry, (2.0 if quantified in QUANTIFIER else 0.5)
    before2 = prefix.token_strings[-3].strip().lower() if len(prefix.token_strings) > 2 else ""
    if before in WORD:
        gate = 1.0
    elif before == "the" and before2 in ("all", "both"):
        gate = 0.8
    else:
        gate = GATE.get(before, 0.1)
    return carry, WORD.get(word, 0.0) * gate

programs.sol:
"""Nominal coordination and enumeration, especially in headings.

Predict mostly zero. At English and/or/& and commas, use the preceding
word's dictionary parts of speech, its length, and the current line's length
and capitalization. Noun readings raise all four responses. Title case and
Markdown headings particularly raise and/&; adjectives, adverbs and long
prose lines reduce the responses. The and response has extra bonuses for
all-title-cased recent words and noun readings in short line prefixes. These
are small fitted formulas, not word-specific values. Other additive/list
markers have fixed responses,
"etc" is negative, and document-initial markers have special fixed values.
Only the last 100 characters of the current document are retained.
"""
import re
from math import exp
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet

READS = ()

# Additive conjunctions: Russian, German, Arabic, Turkish, Indonesian,
# Vietnamese, Chinese, Japanese and Korean.
ADDITIVE = frozenset((
    ' и', ' und', ' و', ' ve', ' dan', ' và',
    '和', '与', '與', '及', 'と', '과', '와', ' 및',
))


@lru_cache(maxsize=16384)
def parts(word):
    p = wordnet.parts_of_speech(word)
    return ('noun' in p, 'adjective' in p, 'adverb' in p)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    text = '' if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    carry = (doc, (text + token)[-100:])

    if token in ADDITIVE:
        return carry, 0.4
    if token == 'や':  # Japanese non-exhaustive list conjunction
        return carry, 1.1
    if token in ('、', '・', '，'):
        return carry, {'、': 0.16, '・': 0.5, '，': 0.06}[token]
    if token.startswith(' وال'):  # Arabic "and the ..."
        return carry, 0.7
    if token in (' AND', ' OR'):
        return carry, 1.2 if token == ' AND' else 0.29
    if token in ('-and', '_and', '/or'):
        return carry, 0.95 if token != '/or' else 0.22
    if token.strip().lower().rstrip('.') == 'etc':
        return carry, -0.5
    if token in ('And', ' And'):
        return carry, 0.15
    if token not in (' and', ' or', ' nor', ' &', ','):
        return carry, 0.0
    if not text:

"""Coordinating conjunctions that join short, title-like phrases.

A layer-1 MLP feature that responds to the word "and" (also "or", "nor", "&" and
their translations) when it joins two items of a short, Title Cased phrase such as
"Diversity and Global Awareness", "Introduction and Outlook", or "Mission, Vision, and
Core Values". The response is strongest when only a few words sit before the
conjunction on its line and those words are capitalized, weaker in longer
clause-like sentences, and near zero when the conjunction follows a comma inside a
sentence. Commas in short title-like lists get a small response.
"""

READS = ()

# Coordinating conjunctions in English and a few other languages.
CONJ = {" and", " AND", " And", " or", " OR", " nor", " &", " und", " и", "和", "与", "と", "や"}
SHORT = 5    # words before the conjunction on its line that make a short phrase
PHRASE = 15  # more words than this and the conjunction is in a sentence, not a phrase


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (words on this line so far, how many of them are Capitalized)
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    n, caps = (0, 0) if (carry is None or new_doc) else carry
    title = caps / n if n else 0.0
    value = 0.0
    if tok in CONJ:
        strength = 1.0 if n <= SHORT else (0.6 if n <= PHRASE else 0.2)
        value = strength * (0.5 + 1.5 * title)
    elif tok == ",":
        value = 0.05 + 0.1 * title if n <= PHRASE else 0.0
    # Update the line's word counts with this token (a newline starts a new line).
    if "\n" in tok:
        n, caps = 0, 0
        tok = tok.split("\n")[-1]
    words = tok.split()
    n += len(words)
    caps += sum(1 for w in words if w[:1].isupper())
    return (n, caps), value

"""Document-start detector for layers.1.mlp.down_proj component 1482.

What it does: this component is silent everywhere except at the first token of a document
(the token right after <|endoftext|>, or the first token of a packed row). There it writes a
large negative value whose size depends on what kind of token opens the document. Every other
position gets 0.

Why the first token only: attention never crosses a document boundary, so a document's first
token attends only to itself. Its activation is then fixed by the token alone, and it matches
the same token run alone to within 2e-5.

Magnitude by kind of first token (means over the vocabulary, as the component reads them):
  - whitespace / newline             about -0.3   (near zero)
  - digit                            about +0.7   (near zero or positive)
  - punctuation or symbols           about -2.4
  - broken UTF-8 byte fragment       about -1.8
  - other non-ASCII text (CJK, etc.) about -2.8
  - ALL-CAPS word                    about -4.7
  - capitalised word                 about -4.3
  - lowercase word with leading space about -3.9
  - lowercase fragment, no space     about -4.6  (word pieces mid-word)
These are the means only; within each kind the token-level spread is large (sd about 2 to 3),
so this rule explains roughly half of the variance at document starts. A full per-token table
explains about 0.93, but it is a list of token ids with no concept behind it.
"""

import re

READS = ()

CLASS_VALUE = {
    "space": -0.3,
    "digit": 0.7,
    "punct": -2.4,
    "broken": -1.8,
    "nonascii": -2.8,
    "allcaps": -4.7,
    "capword": -4.3,
    "space_word": -3.9,
    "fragment": -4.6,
}


def token_class(text):
    """The kind of token a decoded token string is."""
    s = text.strip()
    if s == "":
        return "space"
    if "�" in s:
        return "broken"
    if re.search(r"[0-9]", s) and not re.search(r"[^\W\d_]", s):
        return "digit"
    if not re.search(r"\w", s):
        return "punct"
    if any(ord(c) > 127 for c in s):
        return "nonascii"
    if len(s) > 1 and s.isupper():
        return "allcaps"
    if s[0].isupper():
        return "capword"
    if text.startswith(" "):
        return "space_word"
    return "fragment"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation at the newest position: a document's first token gets its kind's value."""
    starts_document = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if not starts_document:
        return carry, 0.0
    return carry, float(CLASS_VALUE[token_class(prefix.token_strings[-1])])

single CJK tokens whose meaning is "smooth, fluent, fast, unobstructed, convenient,
pleasant" (顺/順, 利, 快, 通, 达/達, 畅/暢, 捷, 爽, 坦, 贯/貫, ...). The value is the

    "愉快": -2.0, "顺利": -2.0, "順利": -2.0, "凯": -1.4, "共享": -1.4, "可达": -1.4,
    "顺": -1.1, "順": -1.1, "快": -1.0, "利": -0.9, "达": -0.9, "通": -0.8, "達": -0.6,
    "便利": -0.9, "方便": -1.0, "高达": -1.0, "率达": -0.9, "荡": -1.0, "惠": -0.9,

DOC_START = 0.18        # first token of a document: average response


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]

"""Respond to locative prepositions and the beginnings of code declarations.

'On' is weaker in dependency/focus phrases and in 'and so on'. Several
languages' on/in words also respond; nearby function words disambiguate
Spanish 'en' and Portuguese 'em'. Code keywords respond at line beginnings
or after modifiers, not usually in prose. Document-initial ASCII alphabetic
pieces have a negative offset, especially the spellings 'int' and 'string'.
Initial space, bullet and opening-docstring tokens have positive reset
responses. Numeric view-count labels have a negative response.
The program retains only 160 characters, resetting at document boundaries.
"""
import re

READS = ()

# Translations of on/in; these are spelling tests, not a language parser.
LOCATIVES = {
    'upon': 0.9, 'в': 0.52, 'на': 0.85, 'auf': 0.55,
    'sur': 0.65, 'på': 1.0, 'na': 0.7, 'w': 0.12,
    'v': 0.07, 'op': 0.2, 'على': 0.6,
}
DECLARATIONS = {
    'public': 1.7, 'private': 1.05, 'protected': 1.5,
    'def': 0.85, 'func': 1.9, 'fn': 1.4, 'function': 1.2,
    'pub': 0.95, 'static': 0.95, 'void': 0.95,
    'override': 0.95, 'inline': 0.95,
}
MODIFIERS = set(('public private protected pub static export async abstract '
                 'final virtual override inline unsafe extern default internal').split())
DEPENDENCE = set(('based base bases basing effect effects impact impacts '
                  'influence influences').split())
SPANISH = set(('el los las del una que por con pero como su sus más es '
               'esta está').split())
FRENCH = set(('le les des du une et est dans pour au aux qui avec vous '
              'nous sur ce').split())
DUTCH = set('het een van voor dat met niet zijn naar'.split())
PORTUGUESE = set('da do das dos não uma com os ao são seu sua'.split())


def activation(token, previous, initial):
    word = token.strip()
    if initial:
        # These are token spellings: they can also begin longer words.
        if token == ' ':
            return 1.276
        if token == '•':
            return 2.094
        if token == '"""\n':
            return 1.555
        if token == 'int':
            return -26.5
        if token == 'string':
            return -17.34
        if word.isascii() and word.isalpha():
            return -0.3 if token[:1].isspace() else -0.56
        return 0.0

    if word in DECLARATIONS:
        # Permit line numbers and diff markers before a declaration.
        line = re.split(r'\n|\\n|[{};]', previous)[-1]
        line = re.sub(r'^\s*[+-]?\s*\d*\s*[|:]?\s*', '', line)
        words = re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]+', line)
        if not line.strip() or words and all(w in MODIFIERS for w in words):
            if word == 'func' and token[:1].isspace():
                return 0.8
            return DECLARATIONS[word]
        return -0.2 if word == 'def' else -0.07
    if word in {'@Override', 'staticmethod', 'classmethod'}:
        return 1.0

    # Ignore word-internal pieces and identifier suffixes.
    if not (token[:1].isspace() or not previous or not previous[-1].isalnum()):
        return 0.0
    lower = word.lower()
    if lower == 'views' and re.search(r'\d+\s*$', previous):
        return -0.53
    if lower in {'w', 'na'} and any(c in 'ąćęłńśźż' for c in previous.lower()):
        return 0.8 if lower == 'w' else 1.1
    if lower == 'on':
        words = re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]+', previous.lower())
        last = words[-1] if words else ''
        if last == 'so':
            return -0.3
        if last in DEPENDENCE or last.startswith(('depend', 'focus')):
            return 0.07
        if last in {'posted', 'posting', 'share', 'shared', 'played'}:
            return 1.25
        return 0.3 if word.isupper() else 0.45 if word.istitle() else 0.63
    if lower == 'на' and word.istitle():
        return 1.15
    if lower in LOCATIVES:
        return LOCATIVES[lower]
    if lower in {'en', 'em'}:
        words = re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]+', previous.lower())
        if lower == 'em':
            return 0.75 if any(w in PORTUGUESE for w in words) else 0.08
        scores = [sum(w in language for w in words)
                  for language in (SPANISH, FRENCH, DUTCH)]
        if not max(scores):
            return 0.1
        return (0.8, 0.05, -0.1)[scores.index(max(scores))]
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    initial = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    previous = '' if initial else carry[1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = activation(token, previous, initial)
    return (doc, (previous + token)[-160:]), value

"""Layer 1 MLP down_proj, component 1484: a "method/function declaration" detector.

What it does, in plain terms:
- Mid-document, it is positive on the words that open a function or method
  declaration when they start a line (public, private, protected, static, void,
  func, fn, function, def, procedure, @Override): about 1.3. The same words used
  mid-sentence or inline (e.g. "class X : public Y", "a function of") are weak, 0.4.
- Mid-sentence prepositions meaning "on/upon" or "in/at" in several languages
  (" on", " upon", " en", " na", " на", " в", " auf", " sur", ...), written with a
  leading space: about 0.6. Words like "in", "of", "to" are 0.
- At the first token of a document (the start of a row, or a new document packed
  mid-row), the activation has no preceding context and is strongly negative for
  bare C/C++/Java type and storage words (void, int, bool, char, static, ...):
  about -20. Other document-first tokens get about -0.4.

Why: this component's activation is large on declaration keywords and on "on"-type
prepositions, and it is near 0 elsewhere. Its contribution to the model output is small.
"""

PREPOSITIONS = {" on", " upon", " en", " na", " на", " в", " auf", " sur", " på", " em",
                " В", " На", " En", " Na", " On", " Upon"}
DECL_WORDS = {"public", "private", "protected", "static", "void", "func", "fn", "function",
              "def", "procedure", "@Override", "staticmethod"}
C_TYPES = {"void", "bool", "int", "char", "float", "double", "long", "short", "unsigned",
           "signed", "static", "private", "public", "virtual", "auto", "typename", "struct",
           "byte", "uint", "string"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    starts_doc = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if starts_doc:
        return carry, (-20.0 if tok in C_TYPES else -0.4)
    word = tok.strip()

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1485, as a short rule-based program.

Almost all of this component's variance is small background noise. Its large
activations come from a few recognisable events, and this program predicts those:

1. Strongest and most reliable, negative: the word "half" or "part(s)" used as a
   division of a whole, right after an ordinal, a number, or "whole"/"entire"
   ("the second half", "the first part", "two parts", "the whole part").
   Activation is about -2 to -6 there. Idioms such as "for the most part" stay near 0.

2. Positive, flags: the second byte-fragment of a flag emoji, written in a
   "country" field ("country of citizenship: 🇴"). The byte-level tokenizer splits
   the emoji into fragments that show as U+FFFD, and the fragment after " �"
   reaches +4 to +12 when a flag is about to be written. Most such positions are
   not flags, so the program predicts the average value, +2.4.

3. Positive, Thai: the vowel-and-tone marks ิ ื ี่ ื่ ี้ written after a Thai
   letter, about +1 on average and up to +8.

Everything else is predicted as 0.
"""

READS = ()

ORDINAL_OR_NUMBER = {
    " first", " second", " third", " fourth", " last", " next", " other", " both",
    " whole", " entire", " each", " one", " two", " three", " four", " five",
    " 1st", " 2nd", " 3rd", " 2", " 3", " 4", " 5",
}
PART_WORDS = {" half", " halves", " part", " parts", "-half", "-part", "_half"}
THAI_VOWEL_TONE = {"ิ", "ื", "ี่", "ื่", "ี้"}
REPLACEMENT = "�"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2] if prefix.position > 0 else ""
    text = prefix.text_prefixes[-1]

        return None, 2.4
    if token in PART_WORDS and previous in ORDINAL_OR_NUMBER:
        return None, -2.5
    if token in THAI_VOWEL_TONE:
        return None, 1.0
    return None, 0.0

"""A surface approximation to a signed Japanese lexical feature.

Recent kana gates responses to expressive punctuation and small named lexical
sets: basic color adjectives, seeing, dwelling, and contrast. Explicit rules
cover reassurance, condition, arrival, attachment, precedence, work-related kanji,
and the kana ま. Other tokens contribute zero. The language signal decays without
kana and resets between documents. These lexemes do not form one semantic topic.
"""
import regex

READS = ()
KANA = regex.compile(r'[\p{Script=Hiragana}\p{Script=Katakana}]')
# The four native Japanese color adjectives: red, blue/green, white, black.
COLOR_ADJECTIVES = frozenset(('赤', '青', '白', '黒'))
SEEING = frozenset(('看', '視', '見'))
DWELLINGS = frozenset(('宅', '屋'))
CONTRAST = frozenset(('逆', '一方'))


def lexical_value(text):
    text = text.strip()
    if not text:
        return 0.0
    chars = set(text)
    if chars <= set('!！?？'):
        return -3.1 if chars & set('！？') else -0.6
    if chars <= set('~〜～'):
        return -5.2
    if text == '…':
        return -3.5
    if chars <= set('.…・') and len(text) > 1:
        return -2.4 if '・' in chars else -0.6
    if text in COLOR_ADJECTIVES:
        return -3.4
    if text in SEEING:
        return 2.4
    if text in DWELLINGS:
        return -3.0
    if text in CONTRAST:
        return -3.3
    if text == '丈夫':  # ending of 大丈夫: "all right / safe"
        return -8.5
    if text == '状':  # condition / situation
        return 4.0
    if text in ('到', '届'):  # arrival / delivery
        return 3.3
    if text == '付':  # attachment
        return 2.2
    if text == '先':  # ahead / earlier
        return 2.1
    if text == '仕':  # service, as in 仕事 (work)
        return -4.0
    if text == '職':  # occupation
        return 3.8
    if text == 'ま':  # the isolated kana syllable "ma"
        return 2.6
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    signal = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else 0.0
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    signal = max(0.95 * signal, float(bool(KANA.search(text))))
    return (doc, signal), signal * lexical_value(text)

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection, component 1486: a weak, mostly lexical detector.

What it does (plain terms):
- Japanese emphasis and sentence-end symbols (！ ？ ～ 〜 … ・ ○ and middle dots) push the
  component negative (about -1).
- A single kanji character that comes right after a hiragana token (for example after the
  particles の, を, に, と, or at the start of a word following kana) pushes it mildly
  positive (about +0.4).
- Everything else, including most kanji and all ASCII, is predicted as 0.

Why: the activation is sparse and heavy-tailed (std 0.095, but reaching -9 and +6 on some
kanji). Its sign depends on which word it is, and no simple rule of the prefix captures that.
These two rules capture only the part concentrated on punctuation and on kanji after kana.
"""

READS = ()

EMPHASIS_SYMBOLS = set("！？～〜…・○··")
NEGATIVE_VALUE = -1.0
KANJI_AFTER_KANA_VALUE = 0.4


def is_kanji(s):
    return len(s) == 1 and "一" <= s <= "鿿"


def is_hiragana(s):
    return len(s) >= 1 and all("぀" <= c <= "ゟ" for c in s)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token in EMPHASIS_SYMBOLS:
        return carry, NEGATIVE_VALUE
    same_doc = len(prefix.token_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if is_kanji(token) and same_doc and is_hiragana(prefix.token_strings[-2]):
        return carry, KANJI_AFTER_KANA_VALUE
    return carry, 0.0

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1487: a document-opening detector.

What it does, in plain terms:
- The colon of a document-opening "Title:" header (a document whose first token is
  "Title" and whose second token is ":") makes a large spike, about +10.2.
- The first token of every document (and the first token of every packed row) gets a
  small negative offset, about -0.36 on average. The exact value there depends on which
  token it is (from about -3.9 to +3), which no simple character class captures, so the
  program uses the average.
- Everywhere else the component is near zero (typically +/-0.05 token-specific noise),
  and the program predicts 0.

Documents are the runs of equal document ids; a new document starts where the id changes
and at position 0 of the row, where attention and positions restart.
"""

READS = ()

TITLE_SPIKE = 10.2
DOC_START_OFFSET = -0.36


def _doc_start(ids, i):
    return i == 0 or ids[i] != ids[i - 1]


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    toks = prefix.token_strings
    t = prefix.position
    if t >= 1 and toks[t] == ":" and toks[t - 1] == "Title" and _doc_start(ids, t - 1):
        return carry, TITLE_SPIKE
    if _doc_start(ids, t):
        return carry, DOC_START_OFFSET
    return carry, 0.0

"""Approximate a mostly quiet component's document-opening transient.

The strongest reproducible signal is a negative value on the first token,
modified by spelling, punctuation, word frequency, and digit magnitude.
A standalone space immediately after a line break is also negative, especially
when the break is written literally as backslash-n. Otherwise predict near zero.
This does not attempt to memorize the substantial token-specific residual.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
QUESTION_WORDS = frozenset('what which who whom whose where when why how'.split())


@lru_cache(maxsize=8192)
def opening_value(s):
    w = s.strip()
    alphabetic = bool(w) and w.isalpha()
    commonness = max(0.0, zipf_frequency(w.lower(), 'en') - 2) / 5 \
        if alphabetic else 0.0
    value = -0.076 - 0.0049 * commonness
    value -= 0.507 * w.startswith('#')
    value -= 0.207 * (alphabetic and w.istitle())
    value += 0.230 * commonness
    value -= 0.171 * alphabetic
    value -= 0.576 * ('/' in w)
    value += 0.166 * (alphabetic and len(w) == 1)
    value += 0.215 * (',' in w)
    value -= 0.413 * ('\\' in w)
    value -= 0.146 * any(ord(c) > 127 for c in w)
    value += 0.418 * (w.lower() in QUESTION_WORDS)
    value -= 0.278 * (bool(s) and s.isspace() and len(s) > 1)
    value -= 0.195 * (s.startswith('<|') and s.endswith('|>'))
    if len(w) == 1 and w in '0123456789':
        value += 0.325 - 0.849 * int(w) / 9
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != document
    if first:
        value = opening_value(s)
    else:
        w = s.strip()
        commonness = max(0.0, zipf_frequency(w.lower(), 'en') - 2) / 5 \
            if w.isalpha() else 0.0
        value = 0.001 - 0.0049 * commonness
        if s == ' ':
            if carry[1].endswith('\\n'):
                value -= 0.66
            elif carry[1].endswith('\n'):
                value -= 0.27

"""A negative R-fragment response in Cyrillic and Slavic Latin spelling.

Recent complete words identify Latin-script Slavic context by dictionary
frequency. Short pieces containing r/р respond, especially after e or i.
Longer pieces, capitals and prefix-like Slavic beginnings respond less.
Two weaker echoes continue into following pieces of the same word.
"""
import re
import unicodedata
from functools import lru_cache
from anyascii import anyascii
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
SLAVIC = ('pl', 'cs', 'sk', 'sl', 'sh')
OTHER = ('en', 'de', 'fr', 'es', 'it', 'pt', 'ro', 'nl', 'sv', 'tr')
MARKS = set('ąćęłńśźżřěůľťĺŕďňčšž')
SCALE = 1.2

@lru_cache(maxsize=32768)
def language(word):
    if len(word) < 2:
        return 0.
    a = max(zipf_frequency(word, lang) for lang in SLAVIC)
    b = max(zipf_frequency(word, lang) for lang in OTHER)
    return max(-1., min(1., (a-b)/2)) if max(a, b) > 3 else 0.


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc or '<|' in s:
        carry = (doc, 0., '', '', 1000, 0., 0.)
    _, evidence, word, previous, distance, tail, tail2 = carry
    for chunk in re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]+|[\W\d_]+', s):
        if chunk.isalpha():
            word = (word + chunk.lower())[-64:]
        elif word:
            evidence = .8*evidence + .2*language(word)
            word = ''
    text = s.strip().lower()
    roman = anyascii(text)
    cyrillic = any('CYRILLIC' in unicodedata.name(c, '') for c in text)
    distance = 0 if any(c in MARKS for c in text) else distance+1
    mode = 1. if cyrillic else max(0., min(1., 2.5*evidence))
    if not cyrillic:
        mode = max(mode, max(0., 1-distance/60))
    continuation = roman.isalpha() and not s[:1].isspace()
    value = 0.
    if roman.isalpha():
        for i, c in enumerate(roman):
            if c != 'r':
                continue
            after = len(roman)-i-1
            before = roman[i-1:i] if i else ''
            score = -.85 if cyrillic else -1.65
            if after == 0:
                score -= .65 if cyrillic else .8
            elif after == 1:
                score -= .15 if cyrillic else .6
            if before == 'e':
                score -= .85 if cyrillic else .65
            elif before == 'i' and cyrillic:
                score -= .6
            if i == 0 and continuation and previous[-1:] in ('e', 'i', 'y'):
                score -= 1.35 if cyrillic else 1.5
            if len(roman) == 4:
                score += .4 if cyrillic else .5
            elif len(roman) >= 5:
                score += .7 if cyrillic else 1.
            if s.strip()[:1].isupper():
                score += .45 if cyrillic else .6
            if s[:1].isspace() and not cyrillic:
                score += .6
            value += mode*score
        if 'r' in roman and roman.startswith(('pr', 'per', 'raz', 'ras')):
            value += mode*(.6 if cyrillic else .8)
    value = min(0., value)
    new_tail = .25*value
    new_tail2 = .25*tail if continuation else 0.
    if continuation:
        value += tail + tail2
    return (doc, evidence, word, roman, distance, new_tail, new_tail2), SCALE*value

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1494 -- the "r inside a short Cyrillic word-fragment" component.

What it does, in plain terms: the component is silent on ordinary text (whole words, numbers,
punctuation, English). It turns negative on the pieces a tokenizer cuts a Russian word into,
when the piece is a short syllable-like fragment containing the letter р: ер, вер, мер, сер,
тер, ор, пор, ир, ар, ров, ра, ру, р. Observed mean activations: ер -3.2, ир -3.0, ор -2.0,
ар -1.3, ра -1.2, ру -0.6. It is strongest on a р that closes a syllable, and weaker on a р
that opens one. It does not respond to the onset cluster пр (при, про, пр), and its response
fades as the fragment gets longer. The Czech letter ř, as a bare fragment, responds like a
strong р.

How the program predicts it. It reads only the newest token's spelling: no state, no table of
token ids.
  1. Lower-case and strip the token. If it is "ř", predict -2.5.
  2. Otherwise it must be all Cyrillic letters, contain р, and contain no "пр"; else 0.
  3. Size by length in letters: 1-2 letters x1.0, 3 x0.75, 4 x0.4, 5 or more x0.15.
  4. Strength: if the р closes a syllable (a vowel directly before it, or the fragment ends in
     р), 2.2 when е or и appears in the fragment, 1.6 for о, 1.2 otherwise; if it opens one, 0.8.

Measured on 3,072 training rows (not eval), the rule explains about 0.23 to 0.28 of the
variance on held-out rows. A lookup of each token's own average would explain about 0.30 to
0.35: it knows that ер is -3.2 and рам is -1.7, which spelling alone does not. The rule keeps
the shape of the response (which fragments, how strong, how it fades with length) without
listing tokens.
"""

READS = ()

VOWELS = "аеиоуыэюяё"


def _is_cyrillic(text):
    return all("Ѐ" <= ch <= "ӿ" for ch in text)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if text == "ř":
        return carry, -2.5
    if not text or "р" not in text or not _is_cyrillic(text) or "пр" in text:
        return carry, 0.0
    n = len(text)
    size = 1.0 if n <= 2 else 0.75 if n == 3 else 0.4 if n == 4 else 0.15
    closes = text.endswith("р") or any(a in VOWELS and b == "р" for a, b in zip(text, text[1:]))
    if not closes:
        return carry, -size * 0.8
    if "е" in text or "и" in text:
        strength = 2.2
    elif "о" in text:
        strength = 1.6
    else:
        strength = 1.2
    return carry, -size * strength

    "With However Although Some Many Here Today I You Our My Also Other Two One Since When While "
    "If By From Not No Such Each Both All Most Several Later Still Now Once Under Despite "

        if '\n' in s:

        if word in {')(', '][', '},{', '){'}: value -= 0.076

'Maybe' and 'perhaps' are strongest after reconsideration cues ('wait',
'alternatively'), weaker after a linking verb, and weaker still when used
as a code name after '::'. Other uncertainty words get smaller positives.

background activations are not modeled.

READS = ()
RECONSIDERING = re.compile(r'\b(?:alternatively|wait)(?:,?\s+but)?[,\s]*$')
LINKING_VERB = re.compile(r'\b(?:is|are|was|were|be|been|being)\s*$')

    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    recent = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]

        elif LINKING_VERB.search(recent.lower()):
            value = 0.71

            value = 0.42
    elif word in {'possibly', '或许'}:
        value = 0.34
    elif word == 'probably':
        value = 0.23
    elif word in {'potentially', 'presumably', 'possibility',
                  'possibilities', 'suppose'}:

    elif word in {'guess', 'wonder'}:
        value = 0.10
    elif token.strip() in {'may', 'might', 'possible'}:
        value = 0.08
    elif word == '也许':

    elif word == '可能':

  * Chinese party/government committee and cadre terms, any token containing 委 (committee,

below zero it goes.

        elif stem.endswith("IPv") or stem.endswith("IPV"):

Kana is evidence of Japanese text. That evidence decays between kana tokens.
In Japanese context predict a negative response on Han tokens, particularly
人 (person) and 者 (person/agent). Other tokens stay near zero, except for a
document-initial value based on script, case and punctuation. Most of the
component's word-specific variation is not covered.
"""
import regex

READS = ()
KANA = regex.compile(r'[\p{Hiragana}\p{Katakana}]')
HAN = regex.compile(r'\p{Han}+')
LATIN = regex.compile(r'\p{Latin}+')
PERSON_KANJI = frozenset('人者')


def initial_value(text):
    """The cold-start response, averaged by broad spelling classes."""
    token = text.strip()
    if regex.search(r'\p{Han}', token):
        return -.14
    if LATIN.fullmatch(token):
        return -.54 if token.isupper() else -.37
    if token.isdigit():
        return -.41
    if not token:
        return -.33
    if not any(c.isalnum() for c in token):
        return -.37 if '\n' in text else -.16
    return -.11


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    start = carry is None or carry[0] != document
    japanese = 0. if start else .94 * carry[1]
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    token = text.strip()
    kana = bool(KANA.search(token))
    if kana:
        japanese = 1.

    value = .0011 + .0214 * kana

        value += initial_value(text)
    if HAN.fullmatch(token):
        value -= .1259 * japanese
        if token in PERSON_KANJI:
            value -= 2.8273 * japanese
    return (document, japanese), float(value)

sums of squared activation in a sample of training text, not a complete
analysis. Most of the unit's variance is in English text and in lexical detail

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection component 1512.

What it does, in plain terms: this component reads "escaped text" and "inline code".

* It fires (+) on a literal backslash-n escape (the two characters \\n, written inside a
  string, as in JSON, C or Python source), and on an 'n' that follows a backslash.
* It fires (+) on backtick characters when they come in a dense run (3+ backticks in the
  last 8 tokens), the way code is quoted as `x` `y` `z` in markdown-like text.
* It goes negative on the indentation that follows an escaped newline (spaces or tabs
  right after a literal \\n), on non-breaking-space indentation, and on a double backslash.

Everything else is predicted as 0. Only the token strings of the current document are
read, a window of the last 8 tokens, so the program is stateless.
"""

READS = ()

WINDOW = 8
ESC_LOOKBACK = 3
BACKSLASH = "\\"
SPACES = " \t\xa0"


def _same_doc(prefix, k):
    return prefix.document_ids[k] == prefix.document_ids[-1]


def _is_escape_newline(prefix, k):
    """Token k is a literal backslash-n (one token '\\n', or 'n' right after a backslash)."""
    tok = prefix.token_strings[k]
    if tok == BACKSLASH + "n":
        return True
    return tok == "n" and k > 0 and prefix.token_strings[k - 1].endswith(BACKSLASH)


def _is_space_run(tok):
    return len(tok) > 0 and all(ch in SPACES for ch in tok)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    tok = prefix.token_strings[t]
    back = [k for k in range(max(0, t - WINDOW), t) if _same_doc(prefix, k)]

    if _is_escape_newline(prefix, t):
        return carry, 1.0

    if "`" in tok:
        dense = sum("`" in prefix.token_strings[k] for k in back) >= 3
        return carry, 1.9 if dense else 0.35

    if _is_space_run(tok):
        after_escape = any(_is_escape_newline(prefix, k) for k in back[-ESC_LOOKBACK:])
        prev = prefix.token_strings[t - 1] if t > 0 else ""
        if after_escape and prev != BACKSLASH + "n" and not _is_space_run(prev):
            return carry, -1.6 if len(tok) >= 3 else -0.7
        if "\xa0" in tok and len(tok) >= 2:
            return carry, -0.9
        if "\t" in tok:
            return carry, -0.4
        return carry, 0.0

    if tok == BACKSLASH + BACKSLASH:
        return carry, -0.9

    return carry, 0.0

"""A partial English adjective-modifier explanation.

Dictionary adjectives get a small lexical prior, with extra weight for identity
and variation, age/time, scale, evaluation, specificity, and addition. Possible
noun/verb/adverb readings, rarity, capitalization and token shape adjust it.
A local grammatical factor boosts quantity contexts and attenuates others.
These rounded coefficients summarize training data, not a full syntactic parser.
The program uses two preceding tokens and resets between documents. Tokens not
classified as content adjectives receive zero. Other languages and fine lexical
exceptions are not explicitly modeled.

from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

ARTICLES = {'a', 'an', 'the'}

POSSESSIVES = set("'s her his its my our their your ’s".split())

DEMONSTRATIVES = {'that', 'these', 'this', 'those'}

QUANTIFIERS = set("""
all another any both each enough every few least less many more most much
multiple no numerous several some various
""".split())

NUMBER_WORDS = set("""
billion eight eighteen eighty eleven fifteen fifty five forty four
fourteen hundred million nine nineteen ninety one seven seventeen seventy
six sixteen sixty ten thirteen thirty thousand three trillion twelve
twenty two
""".split())

ORDINALS = set("""
double eighth eleventh fifth first fourth last next ninth second seventh
single sixth tenth third triple twelfth
""".split())

COPULAS = set("""
am are be became become becomes been being feel feels felt is look looked
looks remain remained remains seem seemed seems was were
""".split())

PRONOUNS = set("""
anything everything he him i it me nothing she something them they us we
what which who you
""".split())

SPECIFICITY = set("""
certain characteristic distinctive individual particular special specific
typical unique
""".split())

ADDITION = set("""
additional complementary extra further supplemental supplementary
""".split())

IDENTITY_VARIATION = set("""
another different distinct diverse equivalent identical other respective
same separate similar various
""".split())

AGE_TIME = set("""
current existing former future last latest new next old previous recent
""".split())

SCALE = set("""
big great greater higher huge large larger little lower massive small
smaller tiny vast
""".split())

EVALUATIVE = set("""

important key necessary nice poor relevant terrible unnecessary useful
valuable wonderful worse worst
""".split())

    'each every either neither all both some any no'.split()
)

             | DETERMINERS | COPULAS | PRONOUNS | set(
    '''and or but as than to for of in on at by with from not if so then
    when where there here once just only also even very too quite rather such'''.split()

)

def properties(token):
    word = token.strip().lower()

    word, pos, adjective = properties(token)

        return carry, 0.0

    strength = 0.092
    strength -= 0.024 * ('noun' in pos)
    strength -= 0.06 * ('verb' in pos)
    strength -= 0.046 * ('adverb' in pos)
    strength -= 0.044 * ('adj.pert' in wordnet.categories(word))

    strength += 0.053 * token[:1].isspace()
    strength += 0.449 * (word in IDENTITY_VARIATION)
    strength += 0.303 * (word in AGE_TIME)
    strength += 0.188 * (word in SCALE)
    strength += 0.209 * (word in EVALUATIVE)

    gate += 0.434 * (pw == 'of')
    gate -= 0.389 * (pw == 'to')
    gate -= 0.212 * (pw in {'very', 'too', 'quite', 'rather', 'so'})
    gate -= 0.79 * (pw in {'more', 'less'})
    gate -= 0.933 * (pw in {'most', 'least'})

    'const': -1.8, 'typedef': -2.0, 'foreach': -2.1,

        elif word == 'with':

        elif word in {'case', 'switch', 'match', 'using'}:

        elif word in TYPES:

        elif word in {'def', 'class', 'function', 'struct', 'public', 'private', 'protected'}:

declaration/statement words (await, typeof, mut, yield, async, const, final, throw,

  1. A keyword table: each keyword gets its typical activation when it is in code
     (negative = the component fires). Words not in the table predict 0.
  2. A code gate: a keyword counts as "in code" if at least 10% of the last 32 tokens
     contain code characters (braces, brackets, parentheses, semicolons, comparison or
     assignment signs, tabs, newlines). Outside code the value is scaled down to 20%.
  3. A few two-word rules: "if not" / "while not" is strongly negative; Go's
     "x := range" is strongly negative; Python's "in range" is slightly positive; a

    des sich auch es im wird wurde werden sind aber oder nach bei noch wie als hat haben dass
    daß sie er wir ich ihr ihre seine sein wenn nur über so vor durch zum zur am vom ob man doch

    unter zwischen aus an in ihm ihnen uns""".split()
)

ENDINGS = frozenset(
    """lich liche licher ig iger igen isch ischen ende enden heit keit ung ungen ten nen chen
    bar sam haft""".split()
)
VOWELS = frozenset("aeiouäöüAEIOUÄÖÜ")
GERMAN_LETTERS = frozenset("äöüßſÄÖÜ")

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (document id, German evidence so far in this document, words so far)
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]

    _, evidence, seen = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]

    elif any(c in GERMAN_LETTERS for c in token):

    seen += 1
    carry = (doc, evidence, seen)

        return carry, 0.0
    gate = min(1.0, max(0.0, (evidence / seen - 0.08) / 0.12))
    if not word.isalpha():

    if word.lower() in WHOLE:

    else:

"""A Scandinavian-context signal, strongest on short word pieces.

Dictionary word frequencies supply language evidence. Two moving averages over
completed words track local context; the current partial word can also supply
evidence. In that context, short word beginnings receive larger estimates;
capitals, longer pieces, grammatical markers, and very common Nordic words
receive smaller ones.
This is an approximation, not a dictionary of model tokens.
"""
import math
import re
from functools import lru_cache
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
NORDIC = ('sv', 'nb', 'da')
OTHER = ('en', 'de', 'nl', 'fr', 'es', 'it', 'pt', 'fi', 'pl', 'cs', 'tr')
GRAMMAR = frozenset(
    'och og att at af av med på till til som är er har hade '
    'ikke inte i'.split()
)

@lru_cache(maxsize=100000)
def frequencies(word):
    nordic = max(zipf_frequency(word, lang) for lang in NORDIC)
    other = max(zipf_frequency(word, lang) for lang in OTHER)
    return nordic, other

@lru_cache(maxsize=100000)
def evidence(word):
    if not word.isalpha():
        return 0.0
    if len(word) == 1:
        return 2.5 if word in 'åæø' else 0.0
    n, o = frequencies(word)
    contrast = n - o
    if any(c in 'åæø' for c in word):
        contrast = max(contrast, 2.5)
    if max(n, o) < 2.5 and contrast < 2.5:
        return 0.0
    return max(-3.0, min(3.0, contrast))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', 0.0, 0.0)
    _, word, slow, fast = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    start = bool(token and (token[0].isspace() or not word))
    for part in re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]+|[\W\d_]+', token):
        if part.isalpha():
            word += part.lower()
        else:
            if word:
                score = evidence(word)
                slow = .83 * slow + .17 * score
                fast = .4 * fast + .6 * score
            word = ''
    carry = (doc, word[-60:], slow, fast)
    w = token.strip().lower()
    latin = any(c in 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzåäöæø' for c in w)
    if not w.isalpha() or not latin:
        return carry, 0.0
    n, _ = frequencies(w)
    local = max(slow, .6 * fast, .25 * evidence(word))
    confidence = max(
        0., (1 / (1 + math.exp(-5 * (local - .65))) - .49) / .51
    )
    strength = (3.76 + .77 * start - 1.75 * (w in GRAMMAR)
                - 1.01 * any(c.isupper() for c in token)
                - 1.46 * min(1., len(w) / 5.)
                - .45 * max(0., n - 5.))
    return carry, float(max(0., confidence * strength))

4. A run of middle-dot leaders ("··") fires at about 5. This was seen in one document

it, and the document labels, so it is causal and needs no other component.

OPENERS = "([{:\"'$"  # tokens that end an opening bracket, quote, colon or "$"

mostly when the word "up" completes the phrasal verb "pick up":

- "up" right after pick / picks / picked / picking, or with one pronoun between
  ("pick him up"): strongly positive (about +13).
- the word "pickup": about +12.
- "up" after take / took / taken / taking: moderately positive (about +4).
- "up" written inside a word after a c or k sound, as in "rec-up-erar" or
  "back-up": positive (about +4.5). Syllables such as "cup", "coup", "recuper",
  "ocup", "kup" also come out positive (+2 to +4); "of" after "cup(s)" is +4.
- "up" after verbs such as give, open, come, put, go, add: negative (about -2.5).
- "with" after "come up" / "give up": negative (about -3).
- any other "up": slightly negative (-0.5).
- everything else: 0.

Predictions are in activation units (the component's own contribution).
"""

READS = ()

PICK = ("pick", "picks", "picked", "picking")
TAKE = ("take", "takes", "took", "taken", "taking")
# Verbs (and a few other words) after which the particle "up" is negative.
NEG_VERB = {
    "come", "came", "coming", "comes", "give", "gave", "giving", "gives", "given",
    "go", "went", "going", "goes", "gone", "open", "opened", "opens", "opening",
    "put", "putting", "roll", "pull", "split", "add", "adds", "adding", "close",
    "primes", "sum", "is", "are", "be", "leading", "lead", "pass", "number",
    "numbers", "divided", "save", "side", "rise", "directories", "cut", "fed",
    "moving", "sums", "summing", "read", "power", "post", "offer", "play",
}
PRONOUNS = {"it", "him", "her", "me", "you", "us", "them", "the", "my", "your", "their"}
UP_TOKENS = {"up", "-up", "ups", "-ups"}
CUP_WORDS = {"cup", "cups", "coup", "pup"}
FRAGMENTS = {"recuper", "recup", "récup", "occup", "ocup", "preocup", "kup", "куп",
             "oup", "upa", "uper", "upid", "upe"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    strs = prefix.token_strings
    cur = strs[-1].strip().lower()
    # Lowercased text of the few tokens before the current one, rejoined so that
    # word pieces such as "p" + "icked" read as one word.
    before = "".join(strs[-7:-1]).lower()
    word_so_far = before.split()[-1] if before[-1:].strip() else ""
    words = before.split()
    prev = words[-1] if words else ""
    prev2 = words[-2] if len(words) > 1 else ""

    if cur == "pickup":
        return carry, 12.0
    if cur in CUP_WORDS:
        return carry, 2.0
    if cur == "with" and prev == "up" and prev2 in NEG_VERB:
        return carry, -3.0
    if cur in FRAGMENTS:
        return carry, 3.5
    if cur == "of" and prev in ("cup", "cups"):
        return carry, 4.0
    if cur in UP_TOKENS:
        if not strs[-1].startswith(" "):
            # "up" written inside a word
            if word_so_far.endswith(PICK):
                return carry, 13.0
            if word_so_far[-1:] in ("c", "k"):
                return carry, 4.5
            return carry, 0.0
        if prev in PICK:
            return carry, 13.0
        if prev2 in PICK and prev in PRONOUNS:
            return carry, 9.0
        if prev in TAKE:
            return carry, 4.0
        if prev in NEG_VERB:
            return carry, -2.5
        return carry, -0.5
    return carry, 0.0

"""An initial-token pulse, with strength depending on broad token classes.

It resets at every document boundary (including a truncated row's start).
Newlines and single spaces are weak; heading/comment markers, declaration
keywords, and English function words are stronger. Later positions are zero.
Class averages approximate, rather than memorize, the large lexical variation.
"""
import regex

READS = ()

# Ordinary spelling and capitalized, unspaced spelling: class averages.
ROLES = (
    (7.7, 7.3, set('a an the'.split())),  # articles
    (7.4, 9.9, set('at by for from in into of on onto over through to under '
                   'upon with without'.split())),  # prepositions
    (5.4, 5.7, set('and or but nor yet so'.split())),  # conjunctions
    (8.2, 13.5, set('if unless when while whenever whereas'.split())),  # conditions
    (5.6, 7.4, set('i you he she it we they me us him her them my your '
                   'his its our their'.split())),  # pronouns
    (4.6, 6.5, set('this that these those some any each every all both '
                   'another other'.split())),  # determiners
    (5.0, 11.4, set('is am are was were be been being have has had do does did '
                    'can could may might must shall should will would'.split())),  # auxiliaries
    (6.8, 12.0, set('how what why where who whom whose which'.split())),  # questions
)
MODULE_DECLARATIONS = set('import package using namespace'.split())
DEFINITIONS = set('class struct enum typedef def function'.split())


def initial_pulse(text):
    word = text.strip()
    lower = word.lower()
    space = text.startswith(' ')
    if text.startswith('<|'):
        return -5.6 if 'endoftext' in text else 7.3
    if not word:
        if any(c in text for c in '\r\n'):
            return 0.1
        return 0.2 if text == ' ' else 4.5
    if word.startswith(('#', '//', '/*', '<?')):
        return 9.8
    if word.isascii() and word.isdigit():
        return 3.7
    if word.isascii() and word.isalpha():
        if len(word) == 1:
            # The indefinite article and first-person pronoun also occupy
            # single-letter tokens; other such tokens are often fragments.
            if lower == 'a' and (space or word.isupper()):
                return 4.6 if space else 5.9
            if word == 'I' and space:
                return 6.1
            return 3.7 if word.isupper() else 1.8
        capitalized = word[0].isupper() and not space
        if not space and lower in MODULE_DECLARATIONS:
            return 10.4 if capitalized else 16.9
        if not space and lower in DEFINITIONS:
            return 6.7 if capitalized else 10.2
        for ordinary, capital, words in ROLES:
            if lower in words:
                return capital if capitalized else ordinary
        return 4.6 if capitalized else 3.6
    if word.isascii():
        value = 3.1 + 0.8 * space
        value -= 1.7 * any(c in text for c in '\r\n')
        value -= 0.9 * (word[0] in '()[]{}')
        value -= 2.4 * (word == ':')
        return value
    return (2.9 - 0.6 * bool(regex.search(r'\p{Script=Han}', word))
            - 1.5 * ('\ufffd' in word))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry != document
    value = initial_pulse(prefix.token_strings[-1]) if first else 0.0
    return document, value

"""A small language-mismatch approximation, with a document-start correction.

Recent completed words vote for a non-English language using dictionary word
frequencies. ASCII letter tokens get a negative adjustment when their spelling
is more frequent in English than in that language, scaled by the context
evidence. Non-Latin writing supplies
non-English context. The first token has a separate spelling/grammar baseline.
This is incomplete: it does not recover individual words' rare large peaks.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import re
import regex
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
LANGUAGES = ('de', 'fr', 'es', 'it', 'pt', 'nl', 'sv', 'nb',
             'da', 'fi', 'pl', 'cs', 'id', 'tr', 'hu')
PRONOUNS = set('i you he she we they it'.split())
DETERMINERS = set('a an the this that these those'.split())


@lru_cache(maxsize=100000)
def frequencies(word):
    return tuple(zipf_frequency(word, lang) for lang in ('en',) + LANGUAGES)


def clamp(x, low, high):
    return max(low, min(high, x))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', (0.0,) * len(LANGUAGES), 0.0, 0.0, 0)
    _, word, scores, nonlatin, count, position = carry
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    for part in re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]+|[\W\d_]+', text):
        if part[0].isalpha():
            word += part
        elif word:
            if len(word) >= 2:
                f = frequencies(word.lower())
                scores = tuple(.9 * old + clamp(x - f[0], -3, 3)
                               for old, x in zip(scores, f[1:]))
                nonlatin = .9 * nonlatin + float(
                    regex.fullmatch(r'\p{Script=Latin}+', word) is None)
                count = .9 * count + 1
            word = ''
    carry = (doc, word, scores, nonlatin, count, position + 1)
    token = text.strip()
    lower = token.lower()
    ascii_word = token.isascii() and token.isalpha()
    value = -.0008
    if position == 0 and text.startswith('<|') and text.endswith('|>'):
        return carry, .015
    if position == 0:
        value += (-.1073 - .0289 * ascii_word + .0787 * text.startswith(' ')
                  - .2792 * (lower in PRONOUNS)
                  - .1535 * (lower in DETERMINERS) - .1734 * token.istitle())
    else:
        value += .0085 * (position < 20)
        if ascii_word:
            f = frequencies(lower)
            language = max(range(len(scores)), key=scores.__getitem__)
            context = clamp(max(max(scores), 1.5 * nonlatin)
                            / max(count, 1), 0, 1.5)
            mismatch = f[0] > f[language + 1] + 1
            value -= .10 * context * mismatch
    return carry, value

"""Layer-1 MLP neuron 1525 (down_proj component 1525), a sparse, mostly negative spike detector.

What it does, in plain terms:
  * At the first token of a document (no context to look at), it goes negative when the token
    is a capitalised word written without a leading space ("The", "This", "They"): about -0.37.
    Other word-like first tokens go weakly negative (about -0.12); everything else is ~0.
  * Mid-document, it spikes negative on a Latin-alphabet capitalised word that appears right
    after a stretch of non-Latin text (code-switching, e.g. an English word inside Japanese or
    Chinese prose): about -0.16.
  * Everywhere else it predicts 0; the real activation there is small noise.
"""

READS = ()

LATIN_WINDOW = 8


def _is_latin_cap_word(s):
    core = s.strip()
    return core[:1].isupper() and core.isascii() and core.isalpha()


def _is_word(s):
    core = s.strip()
    return core.isalpha()


def _non_latin(s):
    return any(ord(c) > 127 for c in s)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    t = prefix.position
    cur = tokens[t]
    # start of this document inside the row
    start = t
    while start > 0 and docs[start - 1] == docs[t]:
        start -= 1
    if t == start:  # first token of a document: its activation depends only on the token
        if _is_latin_cap_word(cur) and not cur.startswith(" "):
            return carry, -0.37
        if _is_word(cur):
            return carry, -0.12
        return carry, 0.0
    # mid-document: a Latin capitalised word right after non-Latin text
    ctx = [x for x in tokens[max(start, t - LATIN_WINDOW):t]]
    if _is_latin_cap_word(cur) and ctx and sum(_non_latin(x) for x in ctx) * 2 > len(ctx):
        return carry, -0.16
    return carry, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1526 -- a document-start detector.

What the component does, as far as a short program can say:

1. First token of each document (the token after <|endoftext|>, or the first
   token of a row). Attention has nothing before it, so the component's value
   there depends only on the token itself. It is positive: about 0.4 for
   ordinary words, about 0.3 for digits, about 0.2 for punctuation, and about
   0.1 for blank or newline-only tokens.
2. The middle-dot pair token "··" (a leader or dot-run), which gives a steady
   0.87 wherever it appears.
3. The "Title:" label opening a document (<|endoftext|>Title:), which gives a
   large negative value, about -3.9. It is rare but very large.

Everywhere else the component is near zero with small, context-dependent
noise (sd about 0.04), which this program does not model.

Main program: track the position inside the current document with the carry,
then apply the rules above.
"""

READS = ()

DOT_RUN = "··"


def first_token_value(s):
    """Activation on a document's first token, by kind of token."""
    body = s.strip()
    if not body:
        return 0.1
    if body.isalpha():
        return 0.4
    if body.isdigit():
        return 0.3
    return 0.2


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        n = 0  # first token of a new document
    else:
        n = carry[1] + 1
    if n == 0:
        value = first_token_value(s)
    elif n == 1 and s == ":" and prefix.token_strings[-2] == "Title":
        value = -3.9
    elif s == DOT_RUN:
        value = 0.87
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return (doc, n), value

"""Approximate the boundary after an English verb's object.

Prepositions, directional particles and -ly words receive a grammatical
score. Object pronouns and noun-like words make it negative, especially
near a possible verb. A short verb + determiner + noun phrase is a stronger
cue. WordNet supplies possible parts of speech, not a full syntactic parse;
unknown alphabetic words are treated as possible names/nouns.

The seven response classes have fitted offsets and strengths. 'Into' and
particles respond strongly; 'of' has a weak reversed response. Other tokens
get zero. Context is limited to 200 characters and resets between documents.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet

READS = ()

PREPOSITIONS = set('''
 to in with as into from for at by on through of using around over without
 until before during against after between under about within via toward
 towards across upon beyond beneath beside behind near among along
'''.split())
PARTICLES = set('''
 out back down off up away together apart forward backward backwards
 ahead aside along
'''.split())
OBJECTS = set('''
 me him her it us them myself yourself himself herself itself ourselves
 themselves this that these those
'''.split())
DETERMINERS = set('''
 a an the this that these those my your his her its our their some any
 each every no all both another such
'''.split())
AUXILIARIES = set('''
 be am is are was were been being have has had do does did will would can
 could should may might must shall
'''.split())
FUNCTION_WORDS = (
    PREPOSITIONS | PARTICLES | OBJECTS | DETERMINERS | AUXILIARIES
    | set('''i he she we they you who whom whose and or but if because when
        where while which than not also very more most such well only so
        '''.split())
)
LINKING_VERBS = set('''
 be become seem appear remain look sound feel occur happen exist depend
 belong consist
'''.split())
ORDINARY_PREPOSITIONS = set('''
 to in on at with as from by using via through
'''.split())


@lru_cache(maxsize=50000)
def grammar(word):
    pos = wordnet.parts_of_speech(word)
    roots = set(wordnet.base_forms(word)) | {word}
    possible_action = (
        word not in FUNCTION_WORDS and 'verb' in pos
        and not roots.intersection(LINKING_VERBS)
    )
    return pos, possible_action


def response(word):
    # Offset and strength for recognizable grammatical word classes.
    if word in ORDINARY_PREPOSITIONS:
        return -0.0604, 0.4796
    if word == 'into':
        return -0.3691, 0.8868
    if word == 'for':
        return -0.0213, 0.2067
    if word == 'of':
        return -0.0240, -0.0404
    if word in PARTICLES:
        return 0.0247, 0.9335
    if word in PREPOSITIONS:
        return -0.0616, 0.2872
    if word.isalpha() and word.endswith('ly'):
        return 0.0131, 0.3067
    return None


def object_score(text):
    clause = re.split(r'[.!?;\n]', text)[-1]
    pieces = re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]+|[^\w\s]', clause)
    while pieces and pieces[-1] in {'`', '"', "'", ')', ']', '}'}:
        pieces.pop()
    previous = pieces[-1].lower() if pieces else ''
    words = [w.lower() for w in pieces if w.isalpha()][-10:]
    earlier = words[:-1] if previous.isalpha() else words
    pos, _ = grammar(previous)
    content_word = previous.isalpha() and previous not in FUNCTION_WORDS
    unknown = content_word and not pos
    nominal = content_word and ('noun' in pos or unknown)
    object_pronoun = previous in OBJECTS
    nearby_verb = any(grammar(w)[1] for w in earlier[-8:])

    # A determiner in the last three words can begin a short object phrase.
    short_object = False
    for distance, word in enumerate(reversed(earlier[-3:]), 1):
        if word in PREPOSITIONS or word in {'and', 'but', 'or'}:
            break
        if word in DETERMINERS:
            head = earlier[-distance-1] if len(earlier) > distance else ''
            short_object = nominal and grammar(head)[1]
            break
    immediate_verb = bool(earlier) and grammar(earlier[-1])[1]
    return (
        0.1125 - 1.1461*object_pronoun - 0.1007*nominal
        - 0.4871*(nominal and nearby_verb) - 0.3325*unknown
        - 1.4875*short_object - 1.1116*(object_pronoun and immediate_verb)
    )


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    text = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    parameters = response(token.strip().lower())
    value = 0.0
    if parameters and (token[:1].isspace() or not text or text[-1:].isspace()):
        offset, strength = parameters
        value = offset + strength*object_score(text)
    return (doc, (text + token)[-200:]), float(value)

            frequency = max(0., log10(counts[word]) + 9)
            for length in range(1, min(30, len(word))):
