def frequency(word, language):
    # Zipf units: 3 means one occurrence per million words.
    return max(0., log10(FREQUENCIES[language].get(word, 1e-9)) + 9)


@lru_cache(maxsize=100000)
def word_evidence(word, language):
    word = word.lower()
    languages = LATIN_LANGUAGES if language == 'latin' else (language,)
    exact = max(frequency(word, lang) for lang in languages)
    gap = max(max(0., COMPLETIONS[lang].get(word, 0.)
                  - frequency(word, lang)) for lang in languages)

    english_gap = max(0., COMPLETIONS['en'].get(word, 0.) - english)
    return english, exact, gap, english_gap


WORD_TAIL = re.compile(r'[^\W\d_]+\Z')


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):

    name = unicodedata.name(letters[0], '')

    language = ('ru' if 'CYRILLIC' in name else
                'el' if 'GREEK' in name else

    if not continued:
        if language != 'latin' and gap > 0.5:
            return carry, 0.049 if familiar <= 2.5 else -0.129
        return carry, 0.008 if len(letters) == 1 else -0.008

    if gap <= 1:

        new_capital = token[0].isupper()
        return carry, 0.19 if len(letters) <= 3 and not new_capital else 0.04

    if english <= 1.5:

            return carry, 1.03 if language == 'ru' else 0.80
        return carry, 0.561 if familiar <= 3.5 else 0.322
    if english <= 2.5:
        return carry, 0.30 if english_gap <= 2.5 else 0.58
    return carry, 0.052 if len(word) <= 3 else 0.205

"""Partial detector of English descriptive qualities, not a full reconstruction.

Texture, temperature, appearance, magnitude, mood and similar qualities are
positive cues. WordNet supplies inflected forms and a few noun/adjective
classes. A decaying count of descriptive words strengthens later descriptions
and the connectors 'and'/'of'. ASCII fragments are joined into words; state
resets at document boundaries. There are no dedicated non-English lexical cues.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import wordnet
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
GROUPS = {
    'touch': '''soft hard smooth rough silky velvety coarse grainy fuzzy
        sticky slippery wet dry damp moist crisp crunchy creamy gritty muddy
        firm tender fluffy brittle supple stiff elastic rigid sleek''',
    'temperature': 'warm cold hot cool chilly freezing frosty icy lukewarm tepid',
    'light_color': '''bright dark pale vivid colorful brilliant radiant dazzling
        golden silvery red blue green white black brown grey gray purple
        yellow orange pink''',
    'geometry': '''deep shallow thick thin wide narrow broad steep flat sharp
        blunt solid hollow dense loose tight round square curved straight''',
    'magnitude': '''vast huge tiny massive enormous immense minute gigantic
        colossal spacious''',
    'beauty': '''beautiful lovely wonderful gorgeous pretty ugly magnificent
        elegant splendid stunning spectacular picturesque charming graceful
        ornate attractive exquisite''',
    'mood': '''calm quiet gentle sad happy merry cheerful fun anxious frightened
        timid brave bold fierce wild angry bitter sweet sour peaceful serene
        tranquil gloomy grim morbid optimistic envious jealous proud humble
        patient persistent eager keen excited nervous restless lazy complacent
        strange weird odd mysterious''',
    'strength': '''strong weak powerful frail sturdy mighty robust feeble
        intense faint vigorous''',
    'complexity': '''complex simple complicated intricate delicate subtle
        confusing clear unclear''',
}
CLASSES = {k: frozenset(v.split()) for k, v in GROUPS.items()}
CLASS_WEIGHTS = {
    'touch': 0.178,
    'temperature': 0.312,
    'light_color': 0.114,
    'geometry': 0.076,
    'magnitude': 0.196,
    'beauty': 0.328,
    'mood': 0.127,
    'strength': 0.206,
    'complexity': 0.08,
}

@lru_cache(maxsize=100000)
def describe(word):
    if not word or not word.isascii() or not word.isalpha():
        return 0., 0.
    bases = set(wordnet.base_forms(word)) | {word}
    flags = {name: bool(bases & words) for name, words in CLASSES.items()}
    score = sum(CLASS_WEIGHTS[name] * hit for name, hit in flags.items())
    # Color names alone do not make a passage descriptively dense.
    count = sum(hit for name, hit in flags.items() if name != 'light_color')
    for kind, weight in [('beauty', .105), ('complexity', .217)]:
        hit = wordnet.is_a(word, kind)
        score += weight * hit
        count += hit
    score += .052 * wordnet.is_a(word, 'atmospheric phenomenon')
    cats = wordnet.categories(word)
    count += wordnet.is_a(word, 'emotion') + ('noun.feeling' in cats)
    pos = wordnet.parts_of_speech(word)
    if 'adjective' in pos:
        score += .019 * max(0., 6 - zipf_frequency(word, 'en'))
        score -= .042 * ('adj.pert' in cats)
    score += .038 * (pos == {'adjective'})
    return score, float(count)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token, doc = prefix.token_strings[-1], prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', 0.)
    _, word, density = carry
    continues = (token and token[0].isascii() and token[0].isalpha() and word)
    tail = re.search('[a-zA-Z]+$', token)
    word = (word + token if continues and token.isascii() and token.isalpha()
            else tail.group() if tail else '').lower()
    score, count = describe(word)
    if token[:1].isspace() and token.strip()[:1].islower():
        score += .055 * count
    connector = token.strip().lower()
    if connector == 'and':
        score += .068 + .160 * density
    elif connector == 'of':
        score += .037 + .133 * density
    elif connector == 'the' or connector == ',':
        score -= .009
    score += .002 + .019 * density + .076 * count * density
    density = min(4., .65 * density + min(2., count))
    if any(c in token for c in '.!?\n'):
        density *= .15
    return (doc, word, density), float(score)

"""A conservative detector of descriptive-word completions.

Negative predictions mark English adjective endings, particularly emotional
-ing participles, and the completion of Han compounds with adjective glosses.
The compound response is larger when the final character alone has fewer
adjective meanings. This is a lexical approximation, not a full POS tagger.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache

import cedict
import regex
import wordfreq
import wordnet

READS = ()


@lru_cache(maxsize=32768)
def description(word):
    """Fraction of translated senses that are adjectives; any quality sense."""
    count = total = 0
    quality = False
    for gloss in cedict.glosses(word):
        gloss = re.sub(r'\([^)]*\)', '', gloss)
        for meaning in gloss.split(';'):
            meaning = meaning.strip()
            if meaning.startswith('to be '):
                meaning = meaning[6:]
            adjective = 'adjective' in wordnet.parts_of_speech(meaning)
            count += adjective
            total += 1
            quality |= adjective and 'adj.pert' not in wordnet.categories(meaning)
    return count / max(1, total), quality


@lru_cache(maxsize=32768)
def english(word, split):
    pos = wordnet.parts_of_speech(word)
    categories = wordnet.categories(word)
    if split:
        if 'adjective' not in pos:
            return -0.01
        if word.endswith('ing'):
            if 'noun' in pos:
                return -0.05
            if 'verb.emotion' in categories:
                return -0.5
            return -0.08 if 'verb.stative' in categories else -0.25
        if ('noun' not in pos and 'adj.pert' not in categories
                and not word.endswith('ed')):
            return -0.07
        return -0.02
    if ('adjective' in pos and word.endswith('ing') and 'noun' not in pos
            and wordfreq.zipf_frequency(word, 'en') < 4.5):
        if ('verb.emotion' in categories or
                {'verb.change', 'verb.cognition'} <= categories):
            return -0.2
    return -0.002


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    previous = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    tail = re.search(r'[A-Za-z]+$', token)
    word = tail.group().lower() if tail else ''
    split = bool(word and len(word) == len(token) and previous
                 and previous[-1].isascii() and previous[-1].isalpha())
    if split:
        word = previous + word
    value = english(word, split) if word else -0.002
    if regex.fullmatch(r'\p{Script=Han}+', token):
        ratio, _ = description(token)
        value = -0.015 - 0.025 * ratio
        if len(token) == 1 and previous:
            pair_ratio, quality = description(previous[-1] + token)
            if quality:
                value = -0.25 * pair_ratio * (2 - ratio)
    return (doc, word if tail else token), float(value)

"""Line-boundary pulses, especially at the beginning of text.

Blank lines after an opening capitalized title or Markdown heading get a
large pulse. Single line endings get a smaller pulse, fading as line breaks
become dense in the document. Declaration headers in source code are also
headings. Sentence punctuation and capitalization distinguish the cases.
Opening words receive a negative offset, especially determiners, possessives,
quantifiers and leading-space prepositions. Other tokens get a small baseline.
State resets at document boundaries.
"""
import math
import re

READS = ()
DECLARATION = re.compile(
    r'^\s*(?:\d+\s+)?'
    r'(?:(?:public|private|protected|export|abstract|final|static|'
    r'sealed|partial|declare|open|data)\s+)*'
    r'(?:class|interface|namespace|struct|enum)\s+\w'
)

POSSESSIVES = set('my your his her its our their'.split())
QUANTIFIERS = set(
    'some any all every each no many much more most few several '
    'both either neither other another'.split()
)
PREPOSITIONS = set(
    'to into onto towards toward from out off in on at under over '
    'above below behind beside near of for about between among '
    'than as with by without through'.split()
)


def opening_value(token):
    word = token.strip()
    lower = word.lower()
    leading = token[:1].isspace()
    if lower in POSSESSIVES:
        return -0.55
    if lower in QUANTIFIERS:
        return -0.7
    if lower in DETERMINERS:
        return -0.35
    if lower in PREPOSITIONS and leading:
        return -0.45
    if token.startswith('<|'):
        return -0.19
    if word[:1].isalpha():
        if word[:1].isupper():
            return -0.07 if leading else -0.19
        return -0.24 if leading else -0.07
    if token.isspace():
        return 0.13
    if word.isdigit():
        return 0.02
    return 0.1

    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:

    _, position, breaks, line, previous_declaration = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = opening_value(token) if position == 0 else 0.004
    declaration = previous_declaration
    if '\n' in token:
        header = line + token.split('\n', 1)[0]
        # A diff hunk may carry the declaration after its location marker.
        header = re.sub(r'^@@.*?@@\s*', '', header.lstrip('+- '))
        declaration = bool(DECLARATION.search(header))
        mark = token.replace('\n', '').replace('\r', '').strip()
        upper = line[:1].isupper()
        space = line[:1].isspace()
        pulse = math.exp(-160 * breaks / (position + 1))
        heading = bool(re.match(r'^#+\s', line))
        if token == '\n\n' or (token == '?\n\n' and heading):
            value = 0.03
            if breaks == 0:
                strength = 1.2 if upper else 0.7 if heading else 0.1
                value += strength * min(1.0, len(line.strip()) / 20)
        elif token in ('.\n', ').\n', '].\n', '."\n', '.”\n'):
            value = 0.005 + pulse * (0.06 if upper else 0.42 if space else 0.25)
        elif token == ' \n':
            value = -0.025 + pulse * (0.18 if upper else 0.5)
        elif token == '\n':
            value = -0.015 + pulse * (0.23 if upper else 0.17 if space else 0.07)
        elif token in ('.\n\n', ' \n\n'):

        else:

        if declaration:
            value = 0.75 if mark in ('{', '):') else 0.3
        elif previous_declaration and not line.strip() and mark == '{':
            value = 0.75
        breaks += token.count('\n')
        line = token.rsplit('\n', 1)[-1]
    else:
        line += token
    return (doc, position + 1, breaks, line, declaration), float(value)
